explain.say: When Elizabeth Bennet first sees Pemberley, the grand estate, she thinks that to be its mistress might be something. A Marxist critic smiles at that moment. Karl Marx said the way a society makes its living shapes its ideas, art and stories. Look at the layers on the board.

explain.say: Start at the bottom: the base. Land and factories, and below it all the question of who owns and who works. In Austen's England, landowners like Mr Darcy, with ten thousand pounds a year, sit at the top. Longbourn is entailed to a male heir, so the Bennet girls must marry. Who owns the land in this story?

explain.say: Now the top layer: culture and novels. Marxists call this the superstructure, and say it carries ideology, ideas that make an unequal order feel natural. Charlotte Lucas marries the ridiculous Mr Collins for a home, and the novel lets you see why. Whose work do we never see at Pemberley?

explain.say: So the same book gives two readings. On the left, a love story where pride is conquered. On the right, a story where marriage moves property and the gentry absorbs the trading Gardiners. Great work. Exam tip: Marxist readings ask who owns, who works and who is silent. Try it on any novel.

faq.a: Marx's model: the economic base, meaning the means and relations of production, shapes the superstructure, meaning law, religion, politics, art and literature.
asks: What is the base and superstructure model?

faq.q: What is ideology in Marxist criticism?
faq.a: A set of ideas and values that make a society's power relations seem natural or inevitable. Literature can carry ideology, and also expose it.

faq.q: How would a Marxist read Pride and Prejudice?
faq.a: By noticing money and property: the entail on Longbourn, Darcy's income, Charlotte's marriage for security, the unseen servants, and an ending that unites landed wealth with a heroine of modest fortune.

faq.q: Who are the key Marxist critics?
faq.a: Georg Lukacs, Walter Benjamin, Raymond Williams, Terry Eagleton and Fredric Jameson are the names you will meet most often.

faq.q: What is a structure of feeling?
faq.a: Raymond Williams's term for the lived, felt experience of a particular time and class, which literature often captures before it is put into ideas.

facts: The Communist Manifesto by Marx and Engels was published in 1848.
In Pride and Prejudice, Mr Darcy is said to have ten thousand pounds a year.
Raymond Williams published Marxism and Literature in 1977.
